label: D1 after rewarded rare a1->S2; peaks mid-episode, fades late
terms: (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 r") ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a2 S2 r") * (tv("action", -2) == 1) * (tv("state", -2) == 2) * (tv("reward", -2) == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 r") * ep_trial ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 r") * (ep_trial ** 2)
explanation: Fires only at D1, and almost only when the previous trial was a1 -> S2 rewarded (rare transition, rewarded): about +1.2 above timing at D1, versus roughly -0.07 after every other pattern. GO and D2 are always 0. The size after a1 S2 r follows an inverted U over the episode: it rises up to about trial 30 and then falls hard late in the episode (the quadratic ep_trial terms). A smaller response (~+0.36) shows up after a2 S2 r when the trial before was a1 S2 r. Things that add little or nothing: a2 S2 r on its own (+0.04), the rest of the trial-before context, the hidden good state, and trials since reversal. Adding the model value at D1 adds less than 0.01 R^2. Every term uses observed variables only. Dev R^2 beyond timing 0.68; the last-trial table alone gives 0.58; ceiling all 0.70.

issues: The main claim holds. The feature fires only at D1 (GO and D2 residuals are exactly 0). After a1 S2 r it sits about +1.2 above baseline, and the original terms reproduce test R^2 beyond timing of 0.667.

The episode-trend claim is roughly right but the wording is off. Fitting one a1 S2 r weight per episode decile gives 1.44, 1.60, 1.62, 1.55, 1.35, 1.00, 0.46, 0.02. The response is nearly flat from trial 0 to 40 and then collapses. It does not really 'rise up to trial 30'.

The claim that 'a2 S2 r on its own adds +0.04 and the rest of the trial-before context adds little' is wrong. A rewarded a2 S2 trial whose trial before was ANY a1 choice gives a large response. Adding (D1)*last_is('a2 S2 r')*(tv('action',-2)==1) to the original terms gets weight +0.82 and raises test R^2 from 0.667 to 0.705, past the 0.70 additive ceiling. The original conjunction (trial before = a1 S2 r) is only one part of this class. Splitting it: after a1 S1 the weight is about +0.86 (+0.62 if that a1 S1 trial was rewarded); after a1 S2 it is about +0.36.

Run on the original terms, misses shows worst-fit windows where a2 S2c r follows an a1 S1c trial: actual 1.03 against predicted 0.07. D1 after a2 S2 r is also the most under-predicted (phase, previous trial) cell. Both point to the same missed class.

Smaller effects: a2 S2 r has a weaker echo when the a1 choice was 2 trials back (weight +0.31). The a2-switch response also follows its own episode trend. A rewarded a2 S2 trial before an a1 S2 r cancels the a1 S2 r response (weight -1.1, but rare).
Not issues: window-start rows where the previous trial is unknown give big single misses (actual 1.9) but add almost nothing (+0.004). Value, hidden good state and since_rev add under 0.002.
